title: Evidence of program execution
quick: Program execution artifacts are traces that show a program ran or was present on a Windows system. No single trace is perfect, so examiners compare several.

sections.title: Why several sources
text: Windows has no single list of every program run. Instead, different features leave small traces as a side effect. Some prove a program ran. Others only show that a file existed. An examiner combines them to build a reliable picture.

sections.title: Common artifacts
text: Each artifact records different details. Learn what each one can and cannot tell you.
points: Prefetch: .pf files in C:\Windows\Prefetch with the program name, run count and recent run times.
UserAssist: registry data on programs a user started from the desktop, with a run count.
ShimCache (AppCompatCache): a list of executables Windows saw, which may not mean they ran.
Amcache: records of programs and their file hashes.
SRUM: a database of app and network usage over time.
BAM: registry entries of recent program use on newer Windows.

sections.title: Prefetch in more detail
text: Prefetch exists to start programs faster. The file name has the program name and a hash of its path, so the same program run from two places gives two files. A file can hold up to eight last run times on Windows 8 and later. Prefetch files can remain after the program is deleted.

compare.title: What each artifact can show
rows: Run count, recent run times, files used
Yes, if started by the user

example: A tool called payload.exe is found in a user's Downloads folder. Prefetch has an entry with a run count of 2 and a last run time. The examiner then checks Amcache for the file hash to look it up on a hash list.
mistakes: Treating ShimCache entries as proof that a program ran.
Forgetting that Prefetch can be turned off or be limited in how many files it keeps.
Reading UserAssist names without knowing they are stored in a scrambled (ROT13) form, so use a tool.
Using one artifact alone to make a conclusion.

terms.meaning: A Windows feature that saves data about a program's start to speed up later starts.
A compatibility record of executable files that Windows has seen.
A hive file with details of programs and their hashes.
How many times a program is recorded as started.

exam.q: Does a ShimCache entry prove execution?
exam.a: No. It shows Windows saw the file. Another artifact is needed to show it ran.

exam.q: Which artifact gives run count and last run times?
exam.a: Prefetch. UserAssist also gives a run count for programs launched by the user.
